cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence
cards.unit: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence
cards.front: Under British colonial rule, about what share of India's population lived in villages and lived off agriculture?
cards.back: India's economy under the British colonial rule remained fundamentally agrarian — about 85 per cent of the country's population lived mostly in villages and derived livelihood directly or indirectly from agriculture
cards.quote: India's economy under the British colonial rule remained fundamentally agrarian — about 85 per cent of the country's population lived mostly in villages and derived livelihood directly or indirectly from agriculture
reasons: review:CONFLICT: keec101 p.5 gives about 85 per cent of the population as living in villages and living off agriculture (colonial rule); keec102 p.27 gives 67.5 per cent dependent on agriculture in 1950. A student holds two answers for the farm-dependent share at independence. Judgement call: held because

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence
cards.unit: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence
cards.front: Why must the colonial relationship be understood to assess India's development since independence?
cards.back: An understanding of the exploitative nature of this relationship is essential for any assessment of the kind and level of development which the Indian economy has been able to attain over the last seven and half decades.
cards.quote: An understanding of the exploitative nature of this relationship is essential for any assessment of the kind and level of development which the Indian economy has been able to attain over the last seven and half decades.
reasons: review:Chapter-framing rationale sentence, not a definition or testable fact.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What percentage of India's population depended on agriculture at independence?
cards.back: At independence, about 75 per cent of the country’s population was dependent on agriculture.
cards.quote: At independence, about 75 per cent of the country’s population was dependent on agriculture.
reasons: review:CONFLICT: keec102 p.24 says about 75 per cent of the population depended on agriculture at independence; p.27 says 67.5 per cent in 1950 falling to 64.9 per cent by 1990 (p.26: 65 per cent in 1990). Keep the specific figures on p.26-27. (conflict sweep, 31 Oct)

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Prices are ____ about the availability of goods.
cards.back: Prices are signals about the availability of goods.
cards.quote: Prices are signals about the availability of goods.
reasons: review:Front has no context (which kind of economy); "signals" has obvious synonyms (indicators, information).

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: The industrial sector and the service sector did not ____ the people working in the agricultural sector
cards.back: The industrial sector and the service sector did not absorb the people working in the agricultural sector
cards.quote: The industrial sector and the service sector did not absorb the people working in the agricultural sector
reasons: review:"absorb" has obvious synonyms (employ, accommodate, accept); fill is not unique.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: No ____ was made between (i) what the public sector alone can do and (ii) what the private sector can also do
cards.back: No distinction was made between (i) what the public sector alone can do and (ii) what the private sector can also do
cards.quote: No distinction was made between (i) what the public sector alone can do and (ii) what the private sector can also do
reasons: review:"distinction" has obvious synonym "difference"; fill is not unique.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: NCERT's examples: what does only the public sector supply, and what does the government run though the private sector manages it well?
cards.back: even now only the public sector supplies national defense. And even though the private sector can manage hotels well, yet, the government also runs hotels.
cards.quote: even now only the public sector supplies national defense. And even though the private sector can manage hotels well, yet, the government also runs hotels.
reasons: review:CONFLICT: keec102 p.32 'even now only the public sector supplies national defense' versus keec103 p.41 'the only industries now reserved for the public sector are part of atomic energy and some railway activities'. Keep the later, more specific reform-chapter statement. (conflict sweep, 31 Oct)

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: The public sector is not meant for earning profits but to promote the ____ of the nation
cards.back: The public sector is not meant for earning profits but to promote the welfare of the nation
cards.quote: The public sector is not meant for earning profits but to promote the welfare of the nation
reasons: review:"welfare" has synonyms (development, good, interest); fill is not unique.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: In the Siricilla powerloom case, why did a power cut mean a cut in weavers' wages?
cards.back: Since the wages of the powerloom workers are linked to the production of cloth, power cut means cut in wages of weavers, who were already suffering from hike in tariff.
cards.quote: Since the wages of the powerloom workers are linked to the production of cloth, power cut means cut in wages of weavers, who were already suffering from hike in tariff.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What did K.R. Narayanan say about GDP as a measure of the progress of a society?
cards.back: There is a consensus in the world today that economic development is not all and the GDP is not necessarily a measure of progress of a society.
cards.quote: There is a consensus in the world today that economic development is not all and the GDP is not necessarily a measure of progress of a society.
reasons: review:Chapter-opening epigraph (K.R. Narayanan); quotation trivia, not a CUET point.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges Facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Human resources like nurses, farmers, teachers, students into ____ like engineers and doctors.
cards.back: Human resources like nurses, farmers, teachers, students into human capital like engineers and doctors.
cards.quote: Human resources like nurses, farmers, teachers, students into human capital like engineers and doctors.
reasons: review:Front is a sentence fragment with no verb or subject; does not stand on its own.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges Facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: We need ____ to produce more human capital out of human resources.
cards.back: We need investment in human capital to produce more human capital out of human resources.
cards.quote: We need investment in human capital to produce more human capital out of human resources.
reasons: review:Blank "investment in human capital" contains words that stay in the front ("human capital"), breaking the blank rule; fill not unique ("investment").

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges Facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: How did education expenditure change during 1952-2020, as a percentage of total government expenditure and of GDP?
cards.back: During 1952-2020, education expenditure as percentage of total government expenditure increased from 7.92 to 16.54 and as percentage of GDP increased from 0.64 to 4.47.
cards.quote: During 1952-2020, education expenditure as percentage of total government expenditure increased from 7.92 to 16.54 and as percentage of GDP increased from 0.64 to 4.47.
reasons: review:Four time-bound statistics (7.92, 16.54, 0.64, 4.47 for 1952-2020); not a memory-worthy CUET point.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges Facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: The level of unemployment among educated youth is the ____.
cards.back: The level of unemployment among educated youth is the highest.
cards.quote: The level of unemployment among educated youth is the highest.
reasons: review:No context (India?); "highest" has synonyms (greatest, maximum) and is guessable from the line.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges Facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: How does NCERT's recap describe investment in human capital formation?
cards.back: Investment in human capital formation is considered as efficient and growth enhancing.
cards.quote: Investment in human capital formation is considered as efficient and growth enhancing.
reasons: review:Front "how does the recap describe investment" invites any paraphrase (beneficial, productive); generic recap sentence of little exam value.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges Facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: Alfred Marshall: why is spending on education profitable as a mere investment, and what does it enable many to do?
cards.back: It will be profitable as a mere investment, to give the masses of people much greater opportunities than they can generally avail themselves of. For by this means many, who would have died unknown, are enabled to get the start needed for bringing out their latent abilities
cards.quote: It will be profitable as a mere investment, to give the masses of people much greater opportunities than they can generally avail themselves of. For by this means many, who would have died unknown, are enabled to get the start needed for bringing out their latent abilities
reasons: review:Quoted opinion of one economist; filler, and the two-part front admits several phrasings.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges Facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: What does the value of information technology depend on greatly (NCERT 4.4)?
cards.back: The value of IT depends greatly on the existing level of economic development.
cards.quote: The value of IT depends greatly on the existing level of economic development.

cards.subject: economics
cards.unit: Current Challenges Facing the Indian Economy
cards.front: NSSO 2011-12: how did youth unemployment compare across rural and urban graduates, rural women graduates and primary-educated youth?
cards.back: the rate of unemployment among youth males who studied graduation and above in rural areas was 19 per cent. Their urban counterparts had relatively less level of unemployment at 16 per cent. The most severely affected ones were young rural female graduates as nearly 30 per cent of them are unemployed. In contrast to this, only about 3-6 per cent of primary level educated youth in rural and urban areas were unemployed.
cards.quote: As per NSSO data, in the year 2011-12, the rate of unemployment among youth males who studied graduation and above in rural areas was 19 per cent. Their urban counterparts had relatively less level of unemployment at 16 per cent. The most severely affected ones were young rural female graduates as nearly 30 per cent of them are unemployed. In contrast to this, only about 3-6 per cent of primary level educated youth in rural and urban areas were unemployed.
reasons: review:Cluster of statistics tied to one survey year (NSSO 2011-12); time-bound, and not must.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What are micro-credit programmes (credit provisions to SHGs)?
cards.back: renovating fund to take up self employement for income generation. Such credit provisions are generally referred to as micro-credit programmes.
cards.quote: renovating fund to take up self employement for income generation. Such credit provisions are generally referred to as micro-credit programmes.

source.section: 5.3 Credit and Marketing in Rural Areas

reasons: review:Back starts mid-sentence ("renovating fund to take up self employement...") so the definition is not self-contained; a definition should be "must", not "good".

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Which eco-friendly technology does NCERT name as essential for sustainable development (5.7)?
cards.back: Efforts in evolving technologies which are eco-friendly are essential for sustainable development and one such technology which is eco-friendly is organic farming.
cards.quote: Efforts in evolving technologies which are eco-friendly are essential for sustainable development and one such technology which is eco-friendly is organic farming.
reasons: review:Front cites "(5.7)" but the sentence is in section 5.6 (Sustainable Development and Organic Farming), page 86.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: How does the fishing community regard the water body, and which water bodies does NCERT name?
cards.back: The fishing community regards the water body as `mother' or `provider'. The water bodies consisting of sea, oceans, rivers, lakes, natural aquatic ponds, streams etc. are, therefore, an integral and life-giving source for the fishing community.
cards.quote: The fishing community regards the water body as `mother' or `provider'. The water bodies consisting of sea, oceans, rivers, lakes, natural aquatic ponds, streams etc. are, therefore, an integral and life-giving source for the fishing community.
reasons: review:Descriptive trivia about fishing communities; two-part front; not must.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What was TANWA (Tamil Nadu Women in Agriculture) and what did it encourage women to do?
cards.back: Tamil Nadu Women in Agriculture (TANWA) was a project initiated in the late 1980s in Tamil Nadu to train women in latest agricultural techniques and in organic farming. It encouraged women to actively participate in raising agricultural productivity and family income.
cards.quote: Tamil Nadu Women in Agriculture (TANWA) was a project initiated in the late 1980s in Tamil Nadu to train women in latest agricultural techniques and in organic farming. It encouraged women to actively participate in raising agricultural productivity and family income.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What do trained women in the Farm Women's Group at Thiruchirapalli make and sell?
cards.back: At a Farm Women's Group in Thiruchirapalli, run by Anthoniammal, trained women are successfully making and selling vermicompost and earning money from this venture.
cards.quote: At a Farm Women's Group in Thiruchirapalli, run by Anthoniammal, trained women are successfully making and selling vermicompost and earning money from this venture.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: How do many Farm Women's Groups build savings, and what do they use the accumulated savings for?
cards.back: Many other Farm Women's Groups are creating savings in their group by functioning like mini banks through a micro-credit system. With the accumulated savings, they promote small-scale household activities like mushroom cultivation, soap manufacture, doll making or other income-generating activities.
cards.quote: Many other Farm Women's Groups are creating savings in their group by functioning like mini banks through a micro-credit system. With the accumulated savings, they promote small-scale household activities like mushroom cultivation, soap manufacture, doll making or other income-generating activities.
reasons: review:Case-story about Farm Women's Groups; micro-credit idea is better carried by an SHG/credit card.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What is gross national product (GNP)?
cards.back: we find that there is a net earning for the country which may be positive (if we have exported more in value terms than imported) or negative (if imports exceeded exports in value terms) or zero (if exports and imports were of the same value). When we add this earning (plus or minus) from foreign transactions, what we get is called the country's gross national product for that year.
cards.quote: we find that there is a net earning for the country which may be positive (if we have exported more in value terms than imported) or negative (if imports exceeded exports in value terms) or zero (if exports and imports were of the same value). When we add this earning (plus or minus) from foreign transactions, what we get is called the country's gross national product for that year.
reasons: review:Back never says what the net foreign earning is added to (GDP is in the previous sentence), and opens mid-sentence ("we find that..."); not a self-contained definition of GNP.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Why is the worker-population ratio higher in rural areas than in urban areas, according to NCERT?
cards.back: People in rural areas have limited resources to earn a higher income and participate more in the employment market.
cards.quote: People in rural areas have limited resources to earn a higher income and participate more in the employment market.
reasons: review:NCERT gives further reasons in the same passage (no schooling or training, drop out to work), so "why" has more than one right answer; back covers only the first.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Ahmedabad's textile mills closed over about 10 years. Where were the workers who lost their jobs driven to?
cards.back: lost their jobs and were driven to the informal sector.
cards.quote: Over this period, approximately over 80,000 permanent workers and over 50,000 non-permanent workers lost their jobs and were driven to the informal sector.
cards.note: Example of informalisation: formal textile jobs lost, workers pushed into the informal sector.
reasons: review:Case-story detail (Ahmedabad textile mills); a CUET student does not need to remember it. The concept is covered by the informal-sector and casualisation cards.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Why do many villagers take urban jobs for some months and return home when the rainy season begins?
cards.back: This is because work in agriculture is seasonal; there are no employment opportunities in the village for all months in the year. When there is no work to do on farms, people go to urban areas and look for jobs.
cards.quote: This is because work in agriculture is seasonal; there are no employment opportunities in the village for all months in the year. When there is no work to do on farms, people go to urban areas and look for jobs.
reasons: review:Narrative explanation/case filler; the seasonal unemployment card carries the point.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Why are the opportunity costs of negative environmental impacts high (NCERT)?
cards.back: Hence the expenditure on health is also rising. To make matters worse, global environmental issues such as global warming and ozone depletion also contribute to increased financial commitments for the government. Thus, it is clear that the opportunity costs of negative environmental impacts are high.
cards.quote: Hence the expenditure on health is also rising. To make matters worse, global environmental issues such as global warming and ozone depletion also contribute to increased financial commitments for the government. Thus, it is clear that the opportunity costs of negative environmental impacts are high.
reasons: review:Back opens with a dangling "Hence" and omits the first reasons on the previous lines (spending on technology and research for new resources, health costs of degraded quality); the front "why" has more answers than the back.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Name six factors contributing to land degradation in India (NCERT lists twelve; nine shown).
cards.back:
loss of vegetation occuring due to deforestation
unsustainable fuel wood and fodder extraction
shifting cultivation
encroachment into forest lands
forest fires and over grazing
non-adoption of adequate soil conservation measures
improper crop rotation
indiscriminate use of agro-chemicals such as fertilisers and pesticides
improper planning and management of irrigation systems
cards.quote: Some of the factors responsible for land degradation are (i) loss of vegetation occuring due to deforestation (ii) unsustainable fuel wood and fodder extraction (iii) shifting cultivation (iv) encroachment into forest lands (v) forest fires and over grazing (vi) non-adoption of adequate soil conservation measures (vii) improper crop rotation (viii) indiscriminate use of agro-chemicals such as fertilisers and pesticides (ix) improper planning and management of irrigation systems
reasons: review:Front asks for "six" while back shows nine of twelve and says "NCERT lists twelve; nine shown"; student cannot tell which items are wanted, and quote omits (x)-(xii). Name all twelve or use a different framing.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: ____ can convert organic matter into compost faster than the normal composting process.
cards.back: Earthworms can convert organic matter into compost faster than the normal composting process.
cards.quote: Earthworms can convert organic matter into compost faster than the normal composting process.
reasons: review:Blank sentence has no topical cue (no mention of composting method or organisms); bacteria, microbes or fungi also fit, so not one right fill.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: How did efforts to meet the challenge of chemical pesticide contamination proceed (Biopest Control)?
cards.back: Even milk, meat and fishes were found to be contaminated. To meet this challenge, efforts are on to bring in better methods of pest control. One such step is the use of pesticides based on plant products. Neem trees are proving to be quite useful. Several types of pest controlling chemicals have been isolated from neem and these are being used.
cards.quote: Even milk, meat and fishes were found to be contaminated. To meet this challenge, efforts are on to bring in better methods of pest control. One such step is the use of pesticides based on plant products. Neem trees are proving to be quite useful. Several types of pest controlling chemicals have been isolated from neem and these are being used.

source.section: 7.5 Strategies for Sustainable Development: Biopest Control

reasons: review:Box case-story (Biopest Control, neem); not a CUET-held line.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What felling rules did Appiko volunteers want contractors and forest officials to follow?
cards.back: Appiko volunteers want the contractors and forest officials to follow certain rules and restrictions. For instance, local people should be consulted when trees are marked for felling and trees within 100 metres of a water source and on a slope of 30 degrees or above should not be felled.
cards.quote: Appiko volunteers want the contractors and forest officials to follow certain rules and restrictions. For instance, local people should be consulted when trees are marked for felling and trees within 100 metres of a water source and on a slope of 30 degrees or above should not be felled.

source.section: Box 7.3: Chipko or Appiko -- What's in a Name?

reasons: review:Case-story (Appiko movement) with specifics (100 m, 30 degrees) that are trivia.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Land degradation factors (x) to (xii): extraction of ground water in excess of what, and which two factors follow?
cards.back: excess of the recharge capacity (xi) open access resource and (xii) poverty of the agriculture-dependent people.
cards.quote: excess of the recharge capacity (xi) open access resource and (xii) poverty of the agriculture-dependent people.

source.section: 7.3 State of India's Environment: Land Degradation

reasons: review:Front depends on numbering (x)-(xii) from a list the card does not show and the quote starts mid-sentence; a student cannot give one answer from the front alone. Rewrite as the full list of land-degradation factors.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What are the three sections of the chapter on Environment and Sustainable Development, in order?
cards.back:
The first part deals with the functions and role of environment.
The second section discusses the state of India's environment
the third section deals with steps and strategies to achieve sustainable development.
cards.quote: this chapter is divided into three sections. The first part deals with the functions and role of environment. The second section discusses the state of India's environment and the third section deals with steps and strategies to achieve sustainable development.
reasons: review:Chapter's own table of contents; not important.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What had already been massively extended in China's rural areas before the reforms?
cards.back:
Basic health services
Before the introduction of reforms, there had already been massive extension of basic health services in rural areas.
cards.quote: Before the introduction of reforms, there had already been massive extension of basic health services in rural areas.
reasons: review:Front is ambiguous: the preceding NCERT sentence also names education infrastructure, so 'what had been massively extended' has more than one defensible answer; name 'basic ___ services' or cite health explicitly.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Why is it essential for developing countries to understand their neighbours' development processes in a globalising world?
cards.back: In the unfolding process of globalisation, this is particularly considered essential by developing countries as they face competition not only from developed nations but also amongst themselves in the relatively limited economic space enjoyed by the developing world.
cards.quote: In the unfolding process of globalisation, this is particularly considered essential by developing countries as they face competition not only from developed nations but also amongst themselves in the relatively limited economic space enjoyed by the developing world.
reasons: review:Chapter rationale for comparing neighbours; framing sentence, not must.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Why is understanding the economies of our neighbourhood required, besides competition in the limited economic space?
cards.back: Besides, an understanding of the other economies in our neighbourhood is also required as all major common economic activities in the region impinge on overall human development in a shared environment.
cards.quote: Besides, an understanding of the other economies in our neighbourhood is also required as all major common economic activities in the region impinge on overall human development in a shared environment.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Income method: GDP ≡ W + P + In + R. What do W, P, In and R stand for?
cards.back:
W, P, In and R are the totals over all households of:
Wi be the wages and salaries received by the i-th household in a particular year. Similarly, Pi, Ini, Ri be the gross profits, interest payments and rents received by the i-th household in a particular year.
cards.quote: Wi be the wages and salaries received by the i-th household in a particular year. Similarly, Pi, Ini, Ri be the gross profits, interest payments and rents received by the i-th household in a particular year.
cards.note: W wages and salaries, P gross profits, In interest payments, R rents.
reasons: review:Back opens with "W, P, In and R are the totals over all households of:", wording that is not NCERT text and not in the quote (paraphrase outside note); quote itself starts mid-sentence at "Wi be".

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Define Personal Income (PI).
cards.back: The part of NI which is received by households. We shall call this Personal Income (PI).
cards.quote: the part of NI which is received by households. We shall call this Personal Income (PI).
reasons: review:Back "The part of NI which is received by households" uses NI, never expanded on the card; it is a lead-in sentence, the tested content is the bold PI formula.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Formula: NDP at factor cost
cards.back: NDPFC = NDPMP - Net Product Taxes - Net Production Taxes
cards.quote: NDPFC = NDPMP - Net Product Taxes - Net Production Taxes
reasons: review:Factor-cost aggregate named in the CUET unit list and a Table 2.4 headed formula; should be must like the GDP at factor cost card.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Formula: GNP at factor cost
cards.back: GNPFC = GNPMP - Net Product Taxes - Net Production Taxes
cards.quote: GNPFC = GNPMP - Net Product Taxes - Net Production Taxes
reasons: review:Factor-cost aggregate named in the CUET unit list and a Table 2.4 headed formula; should be must like the GDP at factor cost card.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What is the Consumer Price Index (CPI)?
cards.back: Consumer Price Index (CPI). This is the index of prices of a given basket of commodities which are bought by the representative consumer.
cards.quote: Consumer Price Index (CPI). This is the index of prices of a given basket of commodities which are bought by the representative consumer.
reasons: review:Price indices (CPI) are not in the CUET 2026 Unit I list (aggregates: factor cost, basic prices, market price; GDP and welfare); spec says no cards for unlisted topics.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: How is the Consumer Price Index of the current year calculated from the base year?
cards.back: We calculate the cost of purchase of a given basket of commodities in the base year. We also calculate the cost of purchase of the same basket in the current year. Then we express the latter as a percentage of the former.
cards.quote: We calculate the cost of purchase of a given basket of commodities in the base year. We also calculate the cost of purchase of the same basket in the current year. Then we express the latter as a percentage of the former.
reasons: review:CPI calculation is outside the CUET 2026 Unit I list; unlisted topic.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What are the retail price and the wholesale price of a commodity?
cards.back: One is the retail price which the consumer actually pays. The other is the wholesale price, the price at which goods are traded in bulk.
cards.quote: One is the retail price which the consumer actually pays. The other is the wholesale price, the price at which goods are traded in bulk.
reasons: review:Retail/wholesale price is outside the CUET 2026 Unit I list. Back starts "One is... The other is..." with no antecedent.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What is the Wholesale Price Index (WPI), and what is it called in the USA?
cards.back: Like CPI, the index for wholesale prices is called Wholesale Price Index (WPI). In countries like USA it is referred to as Producer Price Index (PPI).
cards.quote: Like CPI, the index for wholesale prices is called Wholesale Price Index (WPI). In countries like USA it is referred to as Producer Price Index (PPI).
reasons: review:WPI/PPI is outside the CUET 2026 Unit I list; unlisted topic.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: CPI vs GDP deflator: the difference on the goods covered
cards.back: The goods purchased by consumers do not represent all the goods which are produced in a country. GDP deflator takes into account all such goods and services.
cards.quote: The goods purchased by consumers do not represent all the goods which are produced in a country. GDP deflator takes into account all such goods and services.
reasons: review:CPI vs GDP deflator comparison is outside the CUET 2026 Unit I list; unlisted topic.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: CPI vs GDP deflator: the difference on imported goods
cards.back: CPI includes prices of goods consumed by the representative consumer, hence it includes prices of imported goods. GDP deflator does not include prices of imported goods.
cards.quote: CPI includes prices of goods consumed by the representative consumer, hence it includes prices of imported goods. GDP deflator does not include prices of imported goods.
reasons: review:CPI vs GDP deflator comparison is outside the CUET 2026 Unit I list; unlisted topic.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: CPI vs GDP deflator: the difference on the weights
cards.back: The weights are constant in CPI – but they differ according to production level of each good in GDP deflator.
cards.quote: The weights are constant in CPI – but they differ according to production level of each good in GDP deflator.
reasons: review:CPI vs GDP deflator comparison is outside the CUET 2026 Unit I list; unlisted topic.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Reserve Bank is the only institution which can issue ____.
cards.back: Reserve Bank is the only institution which can issue currency.
cards.quote: Reserve Bank is the only institution which can issue currency.

source.section: 3.4 Policy Tools to Control Money Supply

reasons: review:CONFLICT: leec103 p.42 'Reserve Bank is the only institution which can issue currency'; p.48 says notes are issued by RBI but coins by the Government of India. (conflict sweep, 31 Oct)

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: C̅, representing ____ consumption level of an economy, remains more or less stable over time. However, I̅ has been observed to undergo ____.
cards.back: C̅, representing subsistence consumption level of an economy, remains more or less stable over time. However, I̅ has been observed to undergo periodic fluctuations.
cards.quote: C̅, representing subsistence consumption level of an economy, remains more or less stable over time. However, I̅ has been observed to undergo periodic fluctuations.

source.section: 4.2 Determination of Income in Two-Sector Model

reasons: review:Second blank "periodic fluctuations" has many valid fills (wide/sharp/large fluctuations); only the first blank (subsistence) is guessable. Blank one word only.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: In this model, I̅ is ____ which means, it is the same no matter whatever is the level of income.
cards.back: In this model, I̅ is autonomous which means, it is the same no matter whatever is the level of income.
cards.quote: In this model, I̅ is autonomous which means, it is the same no matter whatever is the level of income.

source.section: 4.3.1 Macroeconomic Equilibrium with Price Level Fixed

reasons: review:"I-bar is ____ which means it is the same no matter the income level": fixed, constant, exogenous and given all fit; "autonomous" is not forced.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What is equilibrium income Y in the two-sector model (4.4)?
cards.back:
Y = (C̅ + I̅) / (1 − c)
Thus, in this situation, ex ante aggregate demand = ex ante aggregate supply,
cards.quote: Thus, in this situation, ex ante aggregate demand = ex ante aggregate supply,

source.section: 4.3.1 Macroeconomic Equilibrium with Price Level Fixed

reasons: review:Quote is only the AD = AS sentence; the answer line Y = (C+I)/(1-c) (eq 4.4, shown as an image equation on p60) is not in the quote, so back is not derived from quote. Quote must carry the equation text.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What is the investment multiplier in terms of c (mpc) and S (equation 4.5)?
cards.back:
Investment multiplier = ΔY/ΔA̅ = 1/(1 − c) = 1/S
where ∆Y is the total increment in final goods output and c = mpc.
cards.quote: where ∆Y is the total increment in final goods output and c = mpc. Observe that the size of the multiplier depends on the value of c .
reasons: review:Answer line (eq 4.5, image equation on p62) is not in the quote; quote holds only the "where dY is..." clause. Back is not derived from quote. Quote the sentence defining the investment multiplier or include the equation text.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: In the AD diagram, how does the line move when A changes, and when c changes?
cards.back:
A changes: parallel shift. c changes: the line swings (slope changes).
When A changes the line shifts upwards or downwards in parallel. When c changes, however, the line swings up or down.
cards.quote: When A changes the line shifts upwards or downwards in parallel. When c changes, however, the line swings up or down.
reasons: review:Front and back write "A" and "A changes"; page 63 shows A with an overbar (autonomous spending). Without the overbar and the word autonomous the front is unclear. Also the line sits in the Paradox of Thrift box.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: An increase (decrease) in autonomous spending causes aggregate output of final goods to increase (decrease) by a larger amount through the ____.
cards.back: An increase (decrease) in autonomous spending causes aggregate output of final goods to increase (decrease) by a larger amount through the multiplier process.
cards.quote: An increase (decrease) in autonomous spending causes aggregate output of final goods to increase (decrease) by a larger amount through the multiplier process.
reasons: review:Blank "multiplier process" includes an interchangeable word (NCERT also says multiplier mechanism/effect); blank only "multiplier".

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Since a major part of revenue expenditure is ____, it cannot be reduced.
cards.back: Since a major part of revenue expenditure is committed expenditure, it cannot be reduced.
cards.quote: Since a major part of revenue expenditure is committed expenditure, it cannot be reduced.
reasons: review:"a major part of revenue expenditure is ____, it cannot be reduced": interest payments, salaries, fixed or non-discretionary expenditure all fit; not one right fill.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: In what does an open economy trade with other nations?
cards.back: An open economy is said to be one that trades with other nations in goods and services and most often, also in financial assets.
cards.quote: Thus, an open economy is said to be one that trades with other nations in goods and services and most often, also in financial assets.
reasons: review:It is NCERT definition of an open economy (the unit subject); definitions are must.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Under the new classification (IMF, BPM6), the BoP is divided into how many accounts, and which?
cards.back: There is a new classification in which the balance of payments have been divided into three accounts – the current account, the financial account and the capital account.
cards.quote: There is a new classification in which the balance of payments have been divided into three accounts – the current account, the financial account and the capital account.
reasons: review:CONFLICT: leec106 p.86 body teaches two BoP accounts (current, capital), with capital account recording all asset transactions; footnote cards (p.86, p.90) say BPM6 has three accounts and moves financial assets to a financial account. Chapter body treats two accounts as the model, so the footnote ca

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Under BPM6, where are transactions in financial assets such as bonds and equity shares placed?
cards.back: The most important change is that almost all the transactions arising on account of trade in financial assets such as bonds and equity shares are now placed in the financial account.
cards.quote: The most important change is that almost all the transactions arising on account of trade in financial assets such as bonds and equity shares are now placed in the financial account.
reasons: review:CONFLICT: leec106 p.86 body teaches two BoP accounts (current, capital), with capital account recording all asset transactions; footnote cards (p.86, p.90) say BPM6 has three accounts and moves financial assets to a financial account. Chapter body treats two accounts as the model, so the footnote ca

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: In a flexible exchange rate system, where is the exchange rate determined?
cards.back: The exchange rate is determined where the demand curve intersects with the supply curve
cards.quote: the exchange rate is determined where the demand curve intersects with the supply curve
reasons: review:Core statement of exchange rate determination, an explicit CUET Unit V item; should be must.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: What is one of the central problems of an economy in terms of production possibilities?
cards.back:
To choose from one of the many production possibilities
Every economy has to choose one of the many possibilities that it has. In other words, one of the central problems of the economy is to choose from one of the many production possibilities.
cards.quote: Every economy has to choose one of the many possibilities that it has. In other words, one of the central problems of the economy is to choose from one of the many production possibilities.
reasons: review:Front is ambiguous: the central problems are what/how/for whom to produce, so a student can reasonably answer 'what to produce'; the only right answer (choose one production possibility) is not pinned by the front.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Formula: what is the slope of the budget line (p1 and p2 are the prices of bananas and mangoes)?
cards.back: The slope of the budget line is – p1/p2.
cards.quote: The slope of the budget line is – p1/p2.
cards.note: p1 = price of bananas (horizontal axis), p2 = price of mangoes (vertical axis).
reasons: review:Front does not say which good is on which axis; slope -p1/p2 holds only with bananas on the horizontal axis and mangoes on the vertical (Fig 2.9). Add the axes.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: The optimum (most preferred) bundle of the consumer would be on the ____.
cards.back: The optimum (most preferred) bundle of the consumer would be on the **budget line**.
cards.quote: The optimum (most preferred) bundle of the consumer would be on the budget line.
reasons: review:Without context, "indifference curve" or "highest indifference curve" are also plausible fills; front is not unique.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Formula: eD = (ΔQ / Q) × (P / ΔP). What do ΔP and ΔQ stand for?
cards.back: Where, ∆P is the change in price of the good and ∆Q is the change in quantity of the good.
cards.quote: Where, ∆P is the change in price of the good and ∆Q is the change in quantity of the good.
cards.note: eD = (percentage change in demand) / (percentage change in price) = (ΔQ/Q) × (P/ΔP).
reasons: review:Formula sits in the front; the card only asks the trivial meaning of dP and dQ and the back never gives the formula (2.16a/b), so the exam-tested formula is not what is recalled.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: If we multiply any value q of output with its corresponding AFC, we always get a ____, namely TFC.
cards.back: If we multiply any value q of output with its corresponding AFC, we always get a constant, namely TFC.
cards.quote: If we multiply any value q of output with its corresponding AFC, we always get a constant, namely TFC.

source.section: Shapes of the Short Run Cost Curves

reasons: review:"we always get a ____, namely TFC": constant and fixed (value/cost) both fit.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: Initially the fall in AFC is greater than the rise in AVC and SAC is still ____.
cards.back: Initially the fall in AFC is greater than the rise in AVC and SAC is still falling.
cards.quote: Initially the fall in AFC is greater than the rise in AVC and SAC is still falling.

source.section: Shapes of the Short Run Cost Curves

reasons: review:Blank "falling" has obvious synonyms (declining, decreasing); not a mark-carrying term.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: But, after a certain level of production, rise in AVC becomes larger than the fall in AFC. From this point onwards, SAC is ____.
cards.back: But, after a certain level of production, rise in AVC becomes larger than the fall in AFC. From this point onwards, SAC is rising.
cards.quote: But, after a certain level of production, rise in AVC becomes larger than the fall in AFC. From this point onwards, SAC is rising.

source.section: Shapes of the Short Run Cost Curves

reasons: review:Blank "rising" has obvious synonyms (increasing, going up); not a mark-carrying term.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.front: In the short run, what must price exceed for a firm to continue to produce?
cards.back: For the firm to continue to produce, in the short run, price must be greater than the average variable cost (p > AVC)
cards.quote: For the firm to continue to produce, in the short run, price must be greater than the average variable cost (p > AVC)
reasons: review:Short-run continue/shut-down condition (p > AVC) is a staple CUET point on profit maximisation; should be must.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Which point on the supply curve is the break-even point of a firm (LRAC, or SAC in the short run)?
cards.back: The point of minimum average cost at which the supply curve cuts the LRAC curve (in short run, SAC curve) is therefore the break-even point of a firm.
cards.quote: The point of minimum average cost at which the supply curve cuts the LRAC curve (in short run, SAC curve) is therefore the break-even point of a firm.

source.section: 4.4.4 The Normal Profit and Break-even Point

reasons: review:Break-even point (normal profit, minimum AC) is a highlighted NCERT concept CUET tests; should be must.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.front: In the price elasticity of supply formula, what are ΔQ and ΔP?
cards.back: ∆Q is the change in quantity of the good supplied to the market as market price changes by ∆P .
cards.quote: Where ∆Q is the change in quantity of the good supplied to the market as market price changes by ∆P .
reasons: review:Front asks what both dQ and dP are, but the quote defines only dQ; dP is never separately defined, so the back does not answer the question. Notation trivia, low value.

cards.subject: economics
cards.front: At any price greater than p*, there will be ____, and at any price lower than p*,there will be ____.
cards.back: At any price greater than p*, there will be excess supply, and at any price lower than p*,there will be excess demand.
cards.quote: At any price greater than p*, there will be excess supply, and at any price lower than p*,there will be excess demand.
reasons: review:p* is undefined in the front (equilibrium price is not named); front does not stand on its own.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.front: When the demand curve shifts, do equilibrium price and quantity change in the same or opposite directions?
cards.back: Notice that the direction of change in equilibrium price and quantity is same whenever there is a shift in demand curve.
cards.quote: Notice that the direction of change in equilibrium price and quantity is same whenever there is a shift in demand curve.
reasons: review:CONFLICT: leec205 p.77 card says price and quantity always move the same way when demand shifts, with no context; p.83 shows that under free entry and exit a demand shift leaves price unchanged. The p.77 card only holds for a fixed number of firms. (conflict sweep, 31 Oct)

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Fig. 5.4(a): both supply and demand curves shift rightward. Effect on price and quantity?
cards.back: both the supply and the demand curves shift rightward leaving price unchanged but a higher equilibrium quantity
cards.quote: both the supply and the demand curves shift rightward leaving price unchanged but a higher equilibrium quantity

source.section: Simultaneous Shifts of Demand and Supply

reasons: review:Figure-specific case: the general result for both curves shifting rightward is that price may rise, fall or stay unchanged, so 'price unchanged' is not derivable from the front. Contradicts the general rule already carded in fact-both-rightward-second-row.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.front: Fig. 5.4(b): supply shifts rightward and demand shifts leftward. Effect on price and quantity?
cards.back: the supply curve shifts rightward and demand curve shifts leftward leaving quantity unchanged but a lower equilibrium price
cards.quote: the supply curve shifts rightward and demand curve shifts leftward leaving quantity unchanged but a lower equilibrium price

source.section: Simultaneous Shifts of Demand and Supply

reasons: review:Figure-specific case: with supply rightward and demand leftward, quantity is ambiguous in general (depends on magnitudes), so 'quantity unchanged' is not derivable from the front. General rule already carded in diff-same-vs-opposite-shifts.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.front: With free entry and exit, each firm will always earn ____
cards.back: With free entry and exit, each firm will always earn normal profit
cards.quote: With free entry and exit, each firm will always earn normal profit

source.section: Market Equilibrium: Free Entry and Exit

reasons: review:"normal profit" vs "zero (economic) profit" are rival fills; front lacks the perfect-competition context.

cards.subject: economics
cards.chapter: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.unit: Theory of Firms under Perfect Competition
cards.front: In equilibrium, the quantity supplied will be determined by the ____ at that price so that they are equal.
cards.back: In equilibrium, the quantity supplied will be determined by the market demand at that price so that they are equal.
cards.quote: In equilibrium, the quantity supplied will be determined by the market demand at that price so that they are equal.

source.section: Market Equilibrium: Free Entry and Exit

reasons: review:Front is not self-contained: 'that price' and 'they' have no antecedent, and 'quantity demanded' or 'demand' are equally valid fills for the blank.
